violation_type.title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §747.1503(a)(4))
violation_type.short_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity
violation_type.typical_finding: During an investigation, it was determined an infant was placed in a play yard in another room unsupervised and sustained minor injuries.

finding_variants.text: During an investigation, it was determined an infant was placed in a play yard in another room unsupervised and sustained minor injuries.

Children under 5yo who were playing at the front porch and carport area were not within complete visual awareness of the caregiver, as the caregiver was inside changing a diaper with the front door open. The ages of the children present required increased supervision, due to lack of the required fenced outdoor space.
Children are left unsupervised at the operation when the provider sleeps and/or naps while children are present in care at the operation.
A child was able to exit the home unnoticed by caregivers and returned to the home by a neighbor.
Children were left unsupervised in the bathroom for approximately 15 minutes resulting in inappropriate behavior by children in care.
During a DFPS investigation, a child in care was able to exit and wandered away from the operation.
